belief: I will never feel well again.
origins: Long illness wears down hope. After many treatments, setbacks, and bad days, the mind starts to treat the present as permanent. Even good days feel like a pause before the next crash.
teaches: “Therefore we do not lose heart.” Scripture says, “He gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak… those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength.” “Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning” (Psalm 30:5). We cannot promise a medical outcome, but we can say that the future is not yours to see and that God holds it. Better and worse days are still ahead, and God is with you in each.
self_statements: I will always feel this way.
There is no hope for recovery.
What is the point of trying?
errors: Believing I will either be fully well or never improve.
Feeling terrible and concluding that I always will.
questions: What has actually changed over time, even a little?
What good days have I had, and what made them better?
What do my doctors honestly say about the outlook?
What does hope mean if the outcome is uncertain?
What does Scripture promise about God’s presence and renewal?
What is one thing that helps today?
truth: I cannot see the future, and neither can my feelings. God gives strength to the weak, and I can hope in Him one day at a time, whatever my health brings.
hw_truths: God gives power to the faint.
Those who wait on Him renew strength.
Weeping may last the night; joy comes.
His mercies are new every morning.
log: Each day, note one thing that went better than expected.
actions: Write down better hours or days.
Discuss realistic goals and what helps.
prayer: Lord, I am weary of being unwell. Give strength to the faint, renew me day by day, and keep hope alive in me whatever comes. Amen.
